summary: The daemon owns notice delivery policy: notice snapshots are written by daemon/runtime on the member bound by a new singleton notice-owner graph declaration, replacing the agent notice-runtime designation. Notice registrations move to reviewed v2 manifests (source 96a618145580c78d6eedd1a9f14ef22adf04542b72cc719ac7d52e4a02cb69d4, snapshot 041f279b64fd2da4884869edcffde8fb88096b80cd1ba8e7d65139c3310f4cf2) without the control family.

replay.detail: Custom folding admits a snapshot fact only when its actor is daemon/runtime, its origin is the member the current notice-owner declaration binds, and that member's bound incarnation (by member key) holds the fact's writer sequence. A missing, conflicting, invalid or ended binding leaves every snapshot unavailable; sources never depend on the binding, so a handover rebuilds snapshots and keeps sources. Revalidation follows the owner declaration (its desired row and intent.desired leaves) and fleet_generation, replacing the agent/run/step/generation liveness triggers and the notice_runtime_binding comparison.

schema.detail: New registry family notice-owner (subject notice-owner/fleet) and intent.desired source kind notice-owner, which changes the claim-registry digest. The agent `notice-runtime` child is removed. Opening a store drops the twelve notice_authority_* triggers and the notice_runtime_binding meta row and installs six notice_owner_* triggers. Reviewed notice manifests are version 2: attention.notice-source drops runtime; attention.notice-snapshot pins runtime to a host/MEMBER reference; attention.notice-control has no manifest and its prefix stays reserved.

rules.detail: Existing graph publishers declare the notice owner: one member name, the bound incarnation's member key, and an authored always-on qualification, all required. Only daemon/runtime writes snapshots and only on the bound member; agents and persons cannot. A daemon cannot author sources. Payload actor fields never confer authority. A trusted fleet member asserting daemon/runtime from the owner's origin is not detected (unchanged fleet-member trust).

compatibility.detail: No tagged release writes v1 notice facts and no notice row is published, so v1 registrations and facts are ignored rather than migrated. The registry digest changes, so existing mismatched-registry guards apply until every member runs a build that knows notice-owner. An older member keeps folding with the v1 agent rules and will not admit v2 registrations; upgrade every member before declaring a notice owner. Graph files that still declare `notice-runtime` on an agent are refused.

manual.detail: After every member runs this build: declare `notice-owner { member "NAME"; member-key "KEY"; always-on }` for an always-on member, with KEY the member_key that member's own fleet status reports, then register the two v2 manifests. Handover edits the same declaration.

recovery.detail: Restore a single current notice-owner declaration naming a current member incarnation; rival leaves resolve by applying a declaration that supersedes both. Reverting this change re-requires an agent notice-runtime designation and v1 registrations; no v2 notice facts survive a revert as admitted.
